clue.text: Prompt but foolish fellow joins the governing body

parts.note: an idiot is a foolish fellow
a board of directors or governors is a governing body

explanation.surface: Someone is quick, yet a silly man has just been made a member of the ruling council.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prompt' looks like an adjective meaning quick, but it is a noun: the cue card held up out of shot for a television presenter.
explanation.definitionFit: A cue card held beside the camera to remind a presenter of their lines is a prompt.

clue.text: Shortage of old copper safety wire

parts.note: D stood for a penny, an old British copper coin, before decimalisation in 1971
the earth wire in a plug is the safety wire that carries stray current to ground

explanation.surface: An electrician complains there is too little old copper safety wire to go round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests the metal of the wire; here it is the coin. The pre-1971 British penny was written d, so 'old copper' gives D.
explanation.definitionFit: A dearth is a scarcity or lack of something.

clue.text: The wife who lived in Oxford?

explanation.surface: A question about where a married woman once had her home in the university city.
explanation.walkthrough: Oxford is not the city but a lace-up shoe: the nursery rhyme tells of an old woman who lived in a shoe. 'The old woman' is also slang for one's wife.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a man's spouse, and the nursery-rhyme figure whose home was a shoe, here an Oxford brogue.

clue.text: Invention by a whiz-kid

explanation.surface: A gadget devised by a young prodigy.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, a child with brains is a whiz-kid; the usual sense is an idea someone has thought up.
explanation.definitionFit: An original idea credited to one person is their creation; taken literally, a clever youngster.

clue.text: After a week, hospital accommodation could be difficult

indicators.note: after places the hospital piece behind the a-and-week pieces

parts.note: a ward is a room of beds in a hospital

explanation.surface: Finding a hospital bed after waiting a week might prove tricky.
explanation.definitionFit: Something awkward is hard to deal with or embarrassing.

clue.text: The platform cuts short Miss Bell

indicators.note: cutting short removes the final letter of the name Miss Bell stands for

parts.note: Daisy Bell is the girl of the old music-hall song 'Daisy, Daisy, give me your answer do'

explanation.surface: A stage interrupts a woman called Miss Bell before she has finished speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cuts short' seems to describe the platform interrupting someone; it tells you to drop the last letter of DAISY.
explanation.definitionFit: A dais is a raised stage at one end of a hall for speakers.

clue.text: Distributes dole to people — like beggars?

explanation.surface: Giving out benefit money to people who resemble beggars.
explanation.walkthrough: As a verb phrase it means gives out; read as 'hands out', it describes beggars holding out their palms.
explanation.definitionFit: Gives out money or goods to a crowd; also describes beggars, palms extended for coins.

clue.text: Prepare to lay the fire but take away, say, eating utensils

explanation.surface: Getting the fire ready, but also collecting cutlery that was used.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take away' looks like removing something; it is a takeaway meal, such as Chinese food, eaten with these sticks. The first sense is cutting kindling.
explanation.definitionFit: Splitting kindling before building a fire, and the paired sticks used for eating East Asian food.

clue.text: Add garnish

explanation.surface: An instruction to put a decoration on a dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'garnish' is not the cook's decoration but a legal term: to garnish wages is to seize them by court order, which is also called to attach them.
explanation.definitionFit: To fasten one thing to another, and in law to seize property or wages by court order.

clue.text: Difficult nautical manoeuvre for a sailor to digest

parts.note: hard means difficult
to tack is to turn a sailing boat's bow through the wind

explanation.surface: A tricky turn at sea is a lot for a seaman to take in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'digest' looks like understanding; it is literal eating, of the hard ship's biscuit sailors lived on.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard ship's biscuit was the staple ration eaten aboard sailing vessels.

clue.text: Exhausted after the dinner guests went home?

definitions.text: after the dinner guests went home?

explanation.surface: The hosts were worn out once their dinner party visitors had left.
explanation.walkthrough: Once the guests have gone the dishes are washed up; the phrase also means finished or worn out.
explanation.definitionFit: Being finished or spent, and having cleaned the plates after a meal.

clue.text: Mate fool who loses pawn

indicators.note: the fool who loses something has a letter dropped from the word

parts.note: a chump is a fool
P is the chess abbreviation for pawn

explanation.surface: A chess game: checkmate for the silly player who has given up a pawn.
explanation.walkthrough: With pawn in the clue, 'Mate' looks like checkmate; it means a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: A chum is a close friend or pal.

clue.text: Retail enterprise specialising in mail order?

explanation.surface: A shop business that concentrates on sending goods by post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mail' is not the post but chain mail armour: a store of chain could be said to deal in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop that is one branch of a group under the same ownership, and whimsically a supplier of chain mail.

clue.text: Performed, but apparently left the stage on a stretcher

definitions.text: apparently left the stage on a stretcher

explanation.surface: An actor gave the show, but seemingly had to be removed from the stage on a stretcher.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase means done or executed; read literally, an injured actor taken off the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Accomplished or executed a task, and literally borne off by others.

clue.text: Supply with pictures of Ulster tail-wagging

indicators.note: wagging shakes the tail about, so these letters move into a new order

explanation.surface: Drawings of a dog from Ulster wagging its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wagging' turns the letters of ULSTER and TAIL into the answer. Ulster is Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: To illustrate a book is to provide drawings or photographs for it.

clue.text: So let it be a Spanish aunt to get a severe mental illness

parts.note: amen, said at the end of a prayer, means so be it
tía is Spanish for aunt

explanation.surface: A religious relative from Spain who ends up seriously disturbed.
explanation.definitionFit: Amentia is an old medical term for profound mental deficiency, distinct from later-onset dementia.

clue.text: Extremely eccentric genius develops idea for more geniuses

indicators.note: develops means these letters grow into a new arrangement
extremely asks for the extremes of eccentric, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A very odd mastermind comes up with a scheme to breed further brilliant minds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'develops' shuffles E and C (the first and last letters of 'eccentric', from 'Extremely') with GENIUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Eugenics is the discredited pseudo-science of improving a population by selective breeding, so breeding cleverer people.

clue.text: It's lace manufactured to be stretchable

indicators.note: manufactured means these letters are made up into something new

parts.note: taken as written, the letters I, T and S

explanation.surface: A description of lace that has been made so it will stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: Elastic material can be pulled longer and springs back.

clue.text: Main limit of Kentish timber and mineral deposit

parts.note: Kent is in the south-east of England, abbreviated SE
ash is a hardwood timber tree
ore is rock containing a valuable mineral

explanation.surface: The chief boundary of a Kent wood and a mine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' looks like chief; it is the old poetic word for the sea, so 'Main limit' is where the sea ends. Kent is the county in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: The coast is the edge of the sea, which poets call the main.

clue.text: Individual acquires a public image

parts.note: a person is an individual

explanation.surface: Someone gains a reputation in the public eye.
explanation.definitionFit: A persona is the character or image someone presents to others.

clue.text: Not the daily habit of retiring women

definitions.text: Not the daily habit of retiring women

parts.words: Not the daily habit of retiring women
parts.note: habit means clothing, retiring means going to bed: what women wear at night rather than in the day

explanation.surface: Shy women do not follow this routine every day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'habit' looks like a routine and 'retiring' like shy; they mean garment and going to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose garment worn in bed, traditionally by women and girls.

clue.text: Promotes to form 6

indicators.note: to form something new, the letters of that answer are rearranged

parts.note: the number points to the answer to 6 Down, the platform

explanation.surface: Raises someone up to the sixth form at school.
explanation.walkthrough: '6' points to the answer at 6 Down, DAIS; 'form' rearranges its letters. In British schools the sixth form is the top two years.
explanation.definitionFit: To aid something is to help it along, to further it.

clue.text: Represent an heroic tale within the bounds of dialect

indicators.note: within puts the tale inside the outer letters of dialect
the bounds of a word are its edges, its first and last letters

parts.note: an epic is a long heroic poem or story

explanation.surface: Telling a saga of heroes using only local speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the bounds of' takes D and T, the first and last letters of 'dialect'; 'within' puts EPIC between them.
explanation.definitionFit: To depict something is to portray it in words or pictures.

clue.text: Small measures for the children

explanation.surface: Little drinks for the kids.
explanation.walkthrough: A tot is a small measure of spirits, so tiny tots are very small drinks; the phrase is also slang for young children.
explanation.definitionFit: Very small shots of spirits, and an affectionate term for little kids.

clue.text: Well-produced paintings

parts.note: read as pictures made with what comes out of a well: paint made with oil, from an oil well

explanation.definitionFit: Pictures done in oil paint; the medium comes from oil wells.

clue.text: Noted drama in which Cicero perhaps anticipates the love of Zeus

indicators.note: anticipates means comes before, so the Cicero piece goes first

parts.note: Cicero was a famous Roman orator, an example of the class
Io was a maiden loved by Zeus in Greek myth, turned into a heifer

explanation.surface: A play in which the Roman statesman foresees the god's romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Noted' means set to musical notes, not famous.
explanation.definitionFit: An oratorio is a large musical work on a sacred story, sung but not staged.

clue.text: Wind up again? Then move back!

explanation.surface: A question about rewinding, then an order to step back.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as RE-COIL, to coil again; the usual sense is to spring back.
explanation.definitionFit: To coil once more, and to flinch or spring backwards.

clue.text: New Testament's solemn declarations

indicators.note: new means freshly made, so these letters take a fresh order

parts.note: the letters as written, including the S

explanation.surface: The solemn pronouncements of the New Testament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New Testament' looks like the Bible's second half; 'New' rearranges the letters of TESTAMENTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal statements are declarations made on record.
